sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Aphrissa, a Columbian who has long resided in Bolívar. Formerly an associate professor at Columbia's Lumines University (La Unida Campus), she is deeply accomplished in the fields of Applied Originium Studies and information and computational science. She resigned from her teaching post after the Great March in Bolívar, and now serves Rhodes Island as a Caster Operator.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Aphrissa shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.16u/L
Although her research requires prolonged contact with Originium, Operator Aphrissa's protective measures have been thorough, and her readings are accordingly close to normal.

'No Oripathy, all test results normal, a perfectly standard diagnostic report—so why do you look so grim?'
'Strange. When exactly did I write this report?'

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
[Reply to the HR Department at Headquarters]
Owing to the current situation, more than half of Lumines University (La Unida Campus)'s Columbian faculty and staff have already withdrawn from Bolívar in successive waves. Fortunately, with the enthusiastic assistance of Ms. Rachel, our liaison at the Academic Affairs Office, we were able to complete the verification of Operator Aphrissa's records without difficulty. It is confirmed that her enrollment, graduation, and employment records match the information she submitted upon joining in every particular—she did indeed enter the university's Applied Originium Studies program at the age of only twelve, obtained her doctorate four years later, and has taught there ever since.
Equally surprising, however, is that this Originium technology researcher—one who might well be called a "genius"—published only three academic papers over her eight years of teaching, and her record of attending academic conferences is sparser still. Granted, Bolívar has long been mired in war and its overall research environment falls short of the Columbian mainland's, but Operator Aphrissa's working habits are, frankly, somewhat worrying.

[Audio Log]
Slacking off? No—Aphrissa's performance in the Engineering Department is all but flawless. Whether it is thorny experimental data analysis, follow-up on equipment development, or subsequent modifications, she handles it all with ease. I hear she even agreed to the Medical Department's request to hold a little class for the children in the ward, called 'Into Originium Science.' See? She hardly seems the sort who has lost interest in research and reuses the same lecture notes for seven years running!
You say she used to teach at Lumines University? At the La Unida Campus, no less? Hsss, then matters get a little complicated. Let me think how to put this... ahem, this story has to start thirty or forty years back.

Lumines University sits in the Max Columbia Special District. One of the first institutions of higher learning founded after the Federation gained independence, it has supplied great numbers of science and engineering graduates to every department and every industry. In the early forties of the last century, the university was formally placed under the jurisdiction of Columbia's Department of Defense, and has been steeped in the colors of the military-industrial complex ever since.
In the mid-sixties, as the strategy of 'Preemptive Containment' was rolled out, the university's Development Planning Office established its first branch campus in La Unida, under the jurisdiction of Bolívar's Coalition Government. The moment the news broke, scholars from every quarter voiced their opposition. Under pressure from within and without, every college of the home campus wrote to the chancellor in turn, and construction of the La Unida Campus was delayed accordingly. Still, backed as it was by the Department of Defense and the Coalition Government, the branch campus offered research funding and terms of employment that were always highly competitive, and many hard-up Columbian researchers still chose to go to La Unida in hopes of realizing their ambitions. By the early eighties, the branch campus was fully on track. Yet because of those early troubles over its founding, no small number of researchers on the Columbian mainland still hold a certain prejudice against the research it produces.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
The enemy has falsely branded this operation an 'evacuation.' They have declared publicly that everyone withdrawing from the north is a civilian. But our checks revealed that a great many True Bolívarian soldiers were in fact mixed in among them. They are massing steadily toward the south, intending to launch terrorist attacks on several of our nomadic cities and settlements.
That is right—yesterday's attack on Tecoma, the containment town serving as our humanitarian aid base, was the dress rehearsal for this conspiracy. Sir, this is no 'evacuation' whatsoever. Please, convey this to the Coalition Assembly without fail: this is a long-premeditated 'march.'
—A recording played at a Columbian military tribunal after the Great March

[Kroos's Operation Log]
As of now, Columbia's Department of Defense has classified the recent series of extreme acts of violence in Bolívar as a large-scale military operation carried out under the cover of civilians. The True Bolívarians have condemned this in the strongest terms. The conflict between the two sides is very likely to escalate once more.
Kroos and Beagle of Reserve Op Team A1, along with some Rhodes Island Operators from the Bolívar office, took part in this operation together. From what we observed, while there were indeed some soldiers among the evacuating column, the bulk of this movement was, beyond doubt, ordinary citizens affected by the blockade in the north.

That night, Beagle, who was to have rendezvoused with us in the southwestern canyon, did not arrive on time. Only two days later did we learn that she and part of her team had made an unscheduled detour to Tecoma, the Coalition Government's hound disease containment town, in order to rescue the patients trapped there. What followed was this: the Blackflow swallowed the entire area, many people went missing as a result, and Beagle was among them.
In a statement released afterward, the Coalition Government claimed that a True Bolívarian force had attacked the town, causing an explosion in the storage depot that ultimately led to the tragedy.
But I do not believe that is what happened at all.

Kroos of Reserve Op Team A1, requesting permission to return to the incident zone to search for Beagle. I can feel it—she must still be in that forest.

Near the river valley, I came across Miss Aphrissa, injured. Fortunately, she had not been infected by the Blackflow at that point. After treating her wounds as best I could, we parted ways.

[Audio Log]
At the time, I had accepted an invitation from a Columbian expedition, joining them as the team's information liaison to survey the area near the Blackflow Forest. Who could have known that the trip would run headlong into the Dossoles unrest and the Great March that swept all of Bolívar... The team was scattered as a result.
My reason for requesting a visit to Rhodes Island? For one thing, to express my gratitude, of course; for another, I wished to find a suitable place to carry on my research. Judging by your expression, something still puzzles you? Heh, ask away. I will answer everything truthfully.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
It was an ordinary afternoon. Aphrissa walked into the ward right on time, as always, ready to teach the children. The moment she stepped through the door, however, she found an unexpected guest among her audience—Miss.Christine. After class, the lady circled her several times with her tail held high. But just as Aphrissa crouched down and reached out to scratch the lady under the chin, she sprang away in an instant and began sizing Aphrissa up, as though appraising her.
Being refused a pat by Miss.Christine is nothing unusual, yet the children in the ward took it to heart for some reason. They jointly wrote a letter to the 'Pet Lovers' Club' right there at Headquarters, hoping to win Teacher Aphrissa a chance to 'pet a small animal to her heart's content.' And so Aphrissa received an invitation and attended that gathering.
At the gathering, a young beckbeast came trotting up to her, tail wagging. Aphrissa let the little thing nuzzle her palm, and the two of them got along famously. Strangely, though, Mousse's 'kitties' were rather wary of her—every time Aphrissa reached out, they would arch their backs at once, slip out of range of her hand, and merely circle around her. Odd indeed: for a Feline, Operator Aphrissa seems singularly unable to win the affection of feline Beast Stewards. Could it be that she carries some scent they dislike? We cannot make sense of it...
In the course of small talk, everyone learned that Aphrissa had once kept a beckbeast. When an Operator casually asked whether she might get another, she only smiled and shook her head.

'That little beckbeast had been at my side for as long as I can remember. The year I turned five, my whole family moved to a small town in central Bolívar. But on the very day we arrived, it ran off into the woods outside town and did not come back by nightfall. The next morning I wanted to go into the woods to look for it, but the grown-ups in town would not allow it—after all, the woods of Bolívar hide far too many secrets. Some warlord's garrison, perhaps, or a black market peddling contraband, or else...'
'Wait! Weren't we talking about beckbeasts? How did this suddenly turn into such a terrifying topic...'

[Rhodes Island Hospital Room Audio Log]
'Have you come to sit in on my class again?
'The sheep are sunning themselves on the deck, and the wolves have gone off somewhere after that silver-white lady. Mr. Emperor will be dropping by Rhodes Island soon with some new records, and also...'
(A long, drawn-out meow)
'Oh, all right, all right. I will answer your question properly.'
(A short, clipped meow)
'The damage is already done; restoring it completely is impossible. But rest assured—Cadejo has found himself again.'
(Satisfied meowing)
'Judging by that reaction... If I may be so bold: might I take your visit as concern for one of your own kind?'
(Puzzled meowing)
'My condition? Heh, the same as yours, my lady. If it is possible, I hope you too might come to see me as a trustworthy... "kindred spirit."'

'Doctor, I still have my doubts about her identity. Her understanding of Originium goes far beyond anything we anticipated. I can sense something dangerous about her, and I'm worried that—
'But she really hasn't stepped out of line anywhere at Headquarters... Fine, we'll leave things as they are for now.
'No! I still want the HR Operators to go over her file one more time! And I'm running another check on ZOOT's encryption while I'm at it!'

[Classified Log]
At Miss Closure's insistence, we conducted a third review of Operator Aphrissa's records. The results were no different from the previous two—there is nothing wrong with her information as such. And yet... it is precisely a file this seamless that arouses suspicion.
Following the thread of her surname, 'Lorenz,' we dug up an old story from Columbian academic circles:
In the late seventies of the last century, a researcher in Applied Originium Studies named 'Robert Lorenz' shook Columbian academia with several groundbreaking papers while barely into his thirties. Surprisingly, however, this scholar in the prime of his life did not remain on the Columbian mainland; instead he accepted a lucrative offer from Lumines University (La Unida Campus) and departed for distant Bolívar. Thereafter the genius fell into one scandal after another. According to what can currently be verified, this 'Lorenz' appears to have stumped for a controversial legislator; to have been suspected of involvement in a private foundation's improper diversion of charitable donations; and even to have intruded upon the family affairs of a leading mainland academic... At first these claims were still regarded as slander against him, and some scholars publicly urged that a scientist's personal choices be viewed rationally. But as word spread that 'Robert Lorenz is conducting illegal experiments in Bolívar,' the young scholar swiftly became the target of universal censure. From then on, this dazzling rising star of academia never again won recognition from the mainland academic world. One day in the late eighties, word reached the outside world that he was believed to have died.
On the materials available to us, we have been unable to establish any definite connection between this Lorenz and Operator Aphrissa. Nor, at present, can we find any clear record of his having started a family in La Unida... The last few years of his life are very nearly a blank. Still, we continue to suspect that some link exists between Operator Aphrissa and this Robert Lorenz.
Lumines University (La Unida Campus)—a campus that has housed two 'Lorenzes' in succession—must surely conceal yet more secrets unknown to the world. The place itself seems to be an exquisite veil draped over some far more classified undertaking.

Doesn't that make for quite the story? If it were possible, I'd love for some big director in Wrankwood to take a liking to it and turn it into a film. It would surely do decent business at the box office.
—A note that appeared on the Doctor's desk

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Open your eyes wide, Toni. Everything you see is real. Don't believe those people's nonsense—you are no 'little Robert,' no 'little Lorenz.' You have a name of your own, and you should have a life of your own.
You were born in Columbia, but because of certain foolish things I did in my youth... and out of my own selfishness, you were quietly taken to Tecoma. Everything that happened afterward you have seen for yourself: once the conjecture was proven and the theory put into practice, this place did not get better—it bred untold suffering and violence instead. I cannot tell you why things turned out this way. I know I have made a grave mistake, and I cannot make amends for it—I never wanted to drag anyone into the mire... I wanted to tell right from wrong again, to find morality, justice, and conscience again, only to discover that these hands of mine, which tried to touch the truth, were long since steeped in sin.
...But you still have a future, Toni. By whatever means, you must leave Tecoma. I do not know what you will be like when you grow up. I would guess you will still be fascinated by science, still burning with enthusiasm for the perfect model. If that is so, then I will pray for you... pray that you will be unlike me, that you will be far better than me, able to answer for all of your research and for every decision you make.
Tecoma is riddled with lies through and through, but your life is not. Toni, someone has truly loved you, and in the years to come there will surely be others who care about who you really are. As for this computing terminal... I thought about it for a long time, and decided in the end to leave it behind. The past has nothing to do with you. Use it from now on to record your own story.
Oh, and the username is your name. So is the password.
